surprises.head: Yaroslav Askarov stole one
surprises.body: Askarov allowed 2 goals on 43 shots, worth 4.8 expected goals: 2.9 fewer than expected. That is more than San Jose’s winning margin, not counting empty-net goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 50 starts.

story.head: Askarov stands on his head
paras: Tim Stützle opened the scoring for the Senators early in the first, but Nolan Allan made it 1-1 for San Jose less than five minutes later. The Sharks’ Igor Chernyshov left late in the period and didn’t return. The next day, he was ruled out with an upper-body injury. Tyler Toffoli put the Sharks ahead 2-1 on the power play midway through the second, and Collin Graf stretched the lead to 3-1 shorthanded less than three minutes later. Jacob Trouba made it 4-1 a little over a minute later. Jordan Spence cut San Jose’s lead to 4-2 early in the third. Zack Ostapchuk added an empty-net goal with three and a half minutes left to make it 5-2. Ivar Stenberg added an empty-net goal with 17 seconds left to make it 6-2.

The score flatters the Sharks: the Senators had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Sens win about seven in ten. Yaroslav Askarov was the difference, stopping 41 of 43. The Senators hit two posts and the crossbar, and the bounces never came. Samuel Ersson stopped 22 of 26 for the Senators. The Sharks improved to 6-4-1, fourth in the Pacific, while the Senators fell to 7-4-0, third in the Atlantic.
